record.original_question: Investigate the geometry of the bilinear scheme Bilin^{r1,r2}_{d1,d2,d3}(A^n): determine its irreducible components, study its singularities, and decide when it is nonreduced.

evidence.quote: Problem XXXVIII. Investigate the geometry of this space.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n, d_1, d_2, d_3, r_1, r_2$ be positive integers and let $\mathbb{A}^n$ denote affine $n$-space over an algebraically closed field $\mathbf{k}$. Consider the bilinear scheme
$$\mathrm{Bilin}^{r_1,r_2}_{d_1,d_2,d_3}(\mathbb{A}^n),$$
whose functor of points sends a $\mathbf{k}$-algebra $R$ to the set of equivalence classes of data
$$(\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{F}_2, \mathcal{F}_3,\; \pi_1, \pi_2,\; \mu),$$
where each $\mathcal{F}_i$ is a locally free quotient of $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$-modules of rank $d_i$ (with $\mathcal{F}_3$ also a quotient compatible with the structure), $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are the corresponding surjections, and
$$\mu : \mathcal{F}_1 \otimes_R \mathcal{F}_2 \longrightarrow \mathcal{F}_3$$
is an $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$-bilinear map such that the images of the natural multiplication maps factor through $\mu$ with appropriate ranks $r_1, r_2$ controlling the dimensions of the spaces of linear factorizations on each side. Equivalently, $\mathrm{Bilin}^{r_1,r_2}_{d_1,d_2,d_3}(\mathbb{A}^n)$ can be realized as a closed subscheme of an appropriate product of Quot schemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$.

Investigate the geometry of $\mathrm{Bilin}^{r_1,r_2}_{d_1,d_2,d_3}(\mathbb{A}^n)$:

(a) Determine its irreducible components. In particular, identify the component(s) parameterizing tuples of points and the totally degenerate locus, and decide for which $(n, d_1, d_2, d_3, r_1, r_2)$ the scheme is reducible.

(b) Describe its singular locus and classify the types of singularities that occur.

(c) Decide for which parameters the scheme is nonreduced, and exhibit nilpotents in the structure sheaf when they exist.
artifact.status_search_result: A recent preprint by Obcowska (arXiv:2601.01648, "The geometry and singularities of the Bilinear scheme") addresses this problem: it represents the bilinear functor as a closed subscheme of a product of Quot schemes, computes its tangent space, identifies a main component (tuples of points) and a totally degenerate locus, and shows reducibility whenever $r_i \ge d \ge 3$. Singularities and reducedness are analyzed in specific small cases (e.g. $\mathrm{Bilin}^{2,2}_{2,2,2}(\mathbb{A}^1)$), so the problem is partially solved but a complete classification of components, singularities, and nonreducedness in general remains open.

status_evidence.title: The geometry and singularities of the Bilinear scheme
status_evidence.snippet: Bilinear functor realized as closed subfunctor of product of Quot schemes; main component (tuples of points) and totally degenerate locus identified; reducible for all n whenever r_i ≥ d ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on components, tangent space, and reducibility of the bilinear scheme have been obtained.
